凶 concerns ill fortune, an unfavorable outcome, or evil. In 凶作 きょうさく, it describes a poor harvest; in 凶悪 (きょうあく), it concerns heinousness rather than agricultural failure. Learn the whole compound rather than translating every 凶 as "bad luck."

凶作 きょうさく — poor harvest; crop failure
凶悪 きょうあく — heinous; atrocious
凶器 きょうき — dangerous or lethal weapon
凶 (きょう) can itself mean bad luck. In fortune-telling, 大凶 (だいきょう) means very bad luck; 凶兆 (きょうちょう) is an ill omen.
悪 also concerns badness or evil, but 凶 is not a replacement for the ordinary adjective 悪い (わるい).
凡 concerns being ordinary; 凸 and 凹 concern raised and sunken shapes. Similar outlines do not make their meanings interchangeable with 凶.

凶作 きょうさく — poor harvest; crop failure
凶作 is a very poor harvest or crop failure. It is a noun describing an agricultural outcome, not a verb meaning "harvest."
今年は米が凶作でした。 (ことしはこめがきょうさくでした。) — This year's rice harvest was very poor.
冷害による凶作が二年続きました。 (れいがいによるきょうさくがにねんつづきました。) — Crop failures caused by cold-weather damage continued for two years.
凶作 does not necessarily mean that nothing at all could be harvested. It can describe a severely reduced yield.

凶 contributes an unfavorable outcome; 作 refers to the crop or yield in this compound. The relationship is modifier + head: a poor crop. The on-readings are キョウ + サク; 作's broader "make" meaning does not turn 凶作 into a general word for bad workmanship.
不作 (ふさく) overlaps in the poor-harvest sense, but also has a broader sense of low-quality work, including literary works. 豊作 (ほうさく), a bumper harvest, is the useful opposite.
作物 (さくもつ) names the crops themselves. 収穫 (しゅうかく) concerns gathering a crop or the resulting yield; it does not by itself say that the harvest was poor.

凶作 focuses on a very poor crop outcome, not every disappointing result or an unlucky event in general. Crop failure can contribute to food shortages, but 凶作 is not itself a statement that a famine occurred.
Dictionary: JMdict, entry 1235440; 作's crop/yield sense: entry 1297240, sense 2. Usage: Digital Daijisen and Nipponica, 凶作.
